name: Shackleton Crater Rim
description: Narrow elevated ridge along Shackleton Crater rim; high solar duty cycle with intermittent Earth visibility obstructed by local polar ridges.

name: Connecting Ridge (Shackleton–de Gerlache)
description: High-standing crest linking Shackleton and de Gerlache craters; sustained sunlight peaks across most of the lunar day with narrow landing tolerances.

name: Malapert Massif Summit
description: Prominent 5 km summit near 0 deg longitude facing Earth; strong direct-to-Earth margin across negative latitude librations with seasonal solar dips.

name: Nobile Crater Rim West
description: Western flank of Nobile Crater; undulating highland horizon creates pronounced solar shadows and variable Earth occultation windows.

name: Apollo 11 — Mare Tranquillitatis
description: Equatorial mare baseline with low flat horizon, continuous high-elevation Earth contact, and classic 14.8-day lunar day/night cycles.

name: Apollo 17 — Taurus-Littrow Valley
description: Deep highland valley flanked by North and South Massifs (16–19 deg horizon peaks), delaying sunrise and advancing sunset despite mid-latitude Earth visibility.
